preconditions.description: The number of cities n is between 1 and 300,000 inclusive.
The number of plans q is between 1 and 300,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= n for a_i in a)
preconditions.description: Each mineral resource a_i in the list a is between 1 and n inclusive.
The length of the list a is equal to the number of cities n.
The number of edges is exactly n-1, forming a tree.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x_i <= n and 1 <= y_i <= n and x_i != y_i for x_i, y_i in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge (x_i, y_i) connects two distinct cities between 1 and n inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u_i <= n and 1 <= v_i <= n and 1 <= l_i <= r_i <= n for u_i, v_i, l_i, r_i in plans)
preconditions.description: Each plan (u_i, v_i, l_i, r_i) specifies cities u_i and v_i between 1 and n inclusive, and resource bounds l_i and r_i such that l_i is less than or equal to r_i.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly q lines, one for each plan.

postconditions.expression: all(output[i] == -1 or (l_i <= output[i] <= r_i and output[i] in resources_between(u_i, v_i) and resources_between(u_i, v_i).count(output[i]) % 2 == 1) for i, (u_i, v_i, l_i, r_i) in enumerate(plans))
postconditions.description: For each plan, the output is either -1 if no valid mineral resource exists, or a valid mineral resource c_i that appears an odd number of times between cities u_i and v_i and satisfies l_i ≤ c_i ≤ r_i.
